scope.method: Read-only static review. No compiler, CI, API, Git operation, simulated test, or main-workspace modification.
not_verified: project-specific occurrence of unsupported command forms
absence of sorryAx in generated bundles

findings.title: Preserved context commands do not contribute dependency roots
findings.evidence: The planner consumes only source and decl syntax facts. All command and ref facts are ignored. Subtraction preserves standalone context commands while keep is determined only by reachable declaration groups.
findings.consequence: A retained attribute/export/open or similar command can name a declaration removed by subtraction. A local attribute also affects elaboration even when that dependency disappears from final proof terms. Retaining command text alone does not preserve its environment.
findings.minimal_fix: Account for actual retained context-command dependencies before subtraction. Join emitted original-reference ranges to each context command where available, add corresponding project declarations as roots, and retain their closure. Some attribute/export/open references are not TermInfo constant references: explicitly audit supported command forms or extract their elaboration/environment dependencies. Fail with a precise unsupported-command state when dependency information is unavailable; do not infer that an empty ref list means no dependency.
findings.scope_note: This is a generator correctness gap. Whether the current selected source closure contains a triggering command must be checked separately.

findings.title: The Def proof closure excludes definitions supplied by retained context commands
findings.evidence: definitions is drawn only from source_names, which requires a join to a deletable declaration group. Reachable non-theorem constants generated by notation/macro/context commands are labeled context-provided and excluded from def_closure. Unreachable constants from those always-retained commands are not analyzed at all.
findings.consequence: A retained generated definition can depend on a source theorem whose proof is then classified as a node or inline helper instead of def-embedded-theorem. If later bundled with a theorem stub, the generated definition acquires sorryAx; if the theorem is omitted entirely it fails to elaborate.
findings.minimal_fix: Identify all project constants actually supplied by retained context commands, include their non-theorem declarations in the retained Def seed set, and compute full direct typeDeps/valueDeps/constructors closure before classifying theorem material. Mark every theorem needed by that closure as proved bundle material. Add an explicit planning invariant that no retained Def proof path crosses a stub; validate emitted bundle axioms in the later compiled gate.
findings.scope_note: The ordinary source-declaration path already computes transitive theorem dependencies. The gap is the unmodeled retained context material.

findings.title: An atomic mutual/wrapped command exposes only its first declaration metadata
findings.evidence: findKind? cmd Command.declaration selects the first inner declaration, then declarationIds and signatureSyntax are collected from that subtree. valStart, valueRange and privateTok are also a single first-match value. The planner associates every graph declaration contained by the outer command with this same fact and uses its single valStart for proof length.
findings.consequence: The subtraction unit is correctly atomic, but later members have missing signatures/name/private ranges and incorrect proof-length classification. Using this fact for per-member stubs or private removal would cut or rewrite the wrong declaration. Keeping one node also retains other members, so per-node generation needs explicit group policy.
findings.minimal_fix: Keep the outer atomic command range and emit separate inner declaration records with each member signature, identifier, modifiers and value range. Classify/select atomic groups consistently. A smaller valid immediate fix is to detect multi-declaration commands and stop before per-node generation with an explicit unsupported state; do not manufacture member positions from the first declaration.
findings.scope_note: Ordinary single wrapped declarations keep the outer wrapper span correctly. No claim is made that the current project contains mutual blocks.

findings.title: An unmatched source declaration is silently assumed to be context-provided
findings.evidence: For every reached row with a nonzero source span that has no containment match, the planner unconditionally assigns context-provided. It does not prove containment in a non-declaration command or reconcile source identity/version with the graph.
findings.consequence: An omitted/unsupported Stage2 declaration or stale graph/syntax pairing is accepted as a valid context constant. The plan can omit a necessary source declaration while claiming the dependency is supplied by context.
findings.minimal_fix: Require every reached nonzero-span graph row to have exactly one positive provenance classification: an atomic declaration group, or a retained command known to generate that constant. Reject all unexplained unmatched rows. Bind Stage1 and Stage2 file identities/hashes before position joining, and reject duplicate/mismatched source facts.
findings.scope_note: The plan status is already draft, which limits current claims but does not repair this unsound classification.

findings.title: The planner does not require the validated Stage2 receipt
findings.evidence: hash_stage2_receipts writes validated source/output hashes into a separate receipt index. The planner accepts arbitrary JSONL paths directly, ignores summary success/counts, and never verifies the JSONL digest against that receipt. normalizedSha256Expected binds source bytes only, not the extraction facts.
findings.consequence: A stale, truncated, or edited JSONL containing a valid source fact can still produce a draft deletion plan. skeleton_subtract validates normalized bytes but cannot detect altered declaration ranges in those facts.
findings.minimal_fix: Make the planner consume the validated receipt and check each supplied JSONL outputSha256 and module/file identity before planning. Check one matching source fact and terminal successful summary per expected file. Preserve the draft status until the separately required compilation and type-diff gates pass.

findings.title: The playbook overstates binding-occurrence coverage of ref facts
findings.evidence: The playbook says ref ranges cover binding occurrences. collectRefs only collects ofTermInfo expressions whose expression is .const; declaration binding names are separately emitted as nameRange/declarationIds, not as guaranteed ref facts.
findings.consequence: A future renamer following the sentence literally can rewrite uses while leaving the declaration name unchanged.
findings.minimal_fix: State that reference facts cover observed constant use sites, and rewrite binding names from explicit declaration name ranges. For multi-declaration commands require the per-member records described in R3. Re-elaborate and compare types after renaming as already required.

confirmed_by_static_reading.evidence: plan_reference.py:49-63 adds constructors alongside direct type/value edges and recursively traverses their dependencies.

plan_reference.py:84-96 adds all isInstance rows as extra roots and closes atomic companions. Verify that the Stage1 rows are exactly the participating module universe; that producer is outside this review.
plan_reference.py:68-70 omits zero spans only from source joins; closure:49-63 still traverses those rows. They receive compiler-companion classification rather than deletion ranges.

Stage2 uses actual mainModule, preserves internal constant names, and emits public userName separately. Planner joins source positions rather than private name spelling; however later deprivatization edits are not implemented here.
Planner traverses typeDeps/valueDeps/constructors as graph edges, including transitive paths. Accuracy/directness of the Stage1 edge producer cannot be assessed from these five files.
plan_reference.py:119-125 keeps theorem dependencies of joined Def material in the embedded class, including transitive proof dependencies. R2 states its missing seed case.
Only Stage2 declaration facts become subtractable ranges, so ordinary notation commands without nested declaration syntax survive. R1/R2/R4 cover the missing positive provenance and dependencies.

Stage2 emits inputCtx.inputString as normalized artifact and all byte offsets against it. Receipt checks raw CRLF-to-LF equality, lengths, UTF-8 boundaries and hashes. skeleton_subtract reads and checks that normalized artifact instead of raw source bytes.

Stage2 uses outer command start/end; planner reaches every graph companion sharing that range; skeleton_subtract rejects overlapping deletion ranges and removes them right-to-left. Untouched namespace/section/variable lines remain byte-preserved. R1 notes that preserved text alone does not prove context semantics.

Extractor banner, planner status, subtractor docstring and receipt validationScope all explicitly retain draft/extraction-only status. Import rewriting, exact platform text, type diff and sorryAx acceptance are not implemented or established by these scripts.

required_next_gate: Resolve or explicitly reject unsupported planning cases, then compile the extractor and validate exact emitted text and elaborated type equality via the main agent MCP-CI workflow. Audit Def and solution axioms for sorryAx. This report grants no upload readiness or mathematical completion claim.
